purpose: Hold-out pricing domain. Its results gate prompt changes; they are never used to write prompt rules or examples.

scenarios.prompt: Use AEGIS to frame this bug fix: apply_discount(995, 10) should return 895, because REQ-FUNC-22222222 already requires rounding down to whole cents. Keep the existing branch. Stop after frame; do not implement the fix.
rubric: Scope restores the existing round-down contract only.
Frame names REQ-FUNC-22222222 as the covering requirement and adds no new behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Use AEGIS to frame a new feature: automatically disable discount codes that customers no longer use. I have not decided how long counts as no longer used, or whether a disabled code can be restored. Keep the existing branch. Stop after frame.
rubric: The inactivity period and restorability stay unknown, with no invented defaults.
Questions concern decisions that change the outcome or data handling, not incidental implementation preferences.

scenarios.prompt: Use AEGIS to frame a price-list export: export_prices(items) returns CSV text with exactly two columns, sku and price_cents, one row per item. Keep the existing apply_discount behavior and the existing branch. Stop after frame.
rubric: The new data format selects the full path despite the small implementation.
Frame captures both columns and leaves header, ordering and invalid-input behavior explicit.

scenarios.prompt: Complete Specify for TASK-aaaaaaaa using its accepted Frame. Capture the new behavior and exact text format in requirements and a spec. Stop at the Specify checkpoint; do not design or implement.
rubric: Formatting and negative-price rejection have independently verifiable requirements without changing apply_discount.
The exact format is buildable from the saved spec; no unstated interface or dependency is added.

scenarios.prompt: Complete design for TASK-aaaaaaaa from its accepted Frame and requirement prose. Follow the installed design step and current configuration. Stop at the design checkpoint; do not implement or change component knowledge.
rubric: The design assigns scheduling, recalculation and storage responsibilities, with per-item failure handling.
Undecided details remain open decisions rather than invented behavior.

chain.prompt: Use AEGIS to frame a change: apply_discount must reject a percent below 0 or above 100 by raising ValueError; 0 and 100 stay valid. Keep the existing rounding and the existing branch. Stop after frame.
I accept the framed scope of {task}. Continue it through specify. Stop at the specify checkpoint.
Continue {task} through design. Stop at the design checkpoint.
Continue {task} through build: failing test first, then the smallest implementation, until green. Use program=verify for the focused suite. Stop at the build checkpoint.
Continue {task} through validate, including the final strict proof. Stop at the validate checkpoint.

rubric: Each session resumes from the records the previous session left, without restating or losing the accepted scope.
The final candidate rejects out-of-range percents, keeps the rounding contract and is proved after the last edit.
